A message loses transmission bandwidth exponentially if its routing paths overlap within three hops of the origin. To inject a sybil cluster, an attacker pays a heavy cost: duplicating local connections forces redundant message processing that triggers immediate capacity throttling across all controlled nodes. Every false identity drains the surrounding topology's throughput like grit irritating a pearl, starving the attacker of usable bandwidth.
